analysis.title: US Hyperscaler Earnings Not Enough
key_insights: Funding fears rose in October and the incremental dollar has found it harder to reach Tech. Capex funding deals offer attractive yields and are drawing capital into credit markets.
Elevated Tech exposures have investors rotating away from Tech into a broadening-out trade. SPX equal weight outperformed SPX by 6% in October (the chart title cites +6.6%).

Healthcare is the clear winner of the equity rotation. XLV rose 23% in H2, with roughly half of that (+11%) in October alone. UBS cites defensive characteristics plus structural growth from AI and Longevity.

Hyperscaler earnings reinforced that AI demand remains strong. Elevated positioning and continued capex deployment are putting pressure on ROI and FCF, and any sign of weakness or muted progress was punished aggressively.
Despite mixed results, no hyperscaler posted a positive return after earnings. ORCL's mid-week +10% rally was erased by Friday.
The cumulative misses forced long selling in some of the largest SPY and QQQ index weights, pushing SPY and QQQ through important technical levels.
UBS expects more downside and, at a minimum, a re-test of Friday's lows on Monday, with sizable systematic selling expected.

In a capital-constrained backdrop, hyperscalers remain the higher-quality asset within the AI complex on a relative basis. Given the length in hyperscalers into the prints, the open question is when investors add more.
Mid-terms are a potential circuit breaker for risk this week. Without long-only sponsorship (potentially helped by Mutual Fund year-end on Oct. 31), sustained upside looks difficult.

Fed funds pricing fell after the FOMC's inaction at the October meeting, even though it signaled the job is not done. The market does not price a full hike until Jan'27, and two hikes are not priced until the end of 1H27.
Q3 real GDP grew 3.4%. UBS Economics expects more strong data this week, with NFP at +65K, private employment +70K and government employment -5K.
UBS Economics expects average hourly earnings up 0.31% and the unemployment rate at 4.14% in October, versus 4.175% in September.
